EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The fragile US-Iran ceasefire has been unilaterally extended by President Trump, yet negotiations are stalled as Iran refuses to participate until the US naval blockade of its ports is lifted. This diplomatic impasse is coupled with continued US military actions, including the seizure of Iranian-linked tankers, and retaliatory strikes and warnings from both Iran and its proxies, significantly elevating regional escalation risks.

IRAN
Military operations against Iran include the US military seizing two oil tankers, "Tiffany" and "Touska," in the Indian Ocean and Sea of Oman, citing illicit material support. President Trump claims the US has destroyed 13,000 targets in Iran, including nuclear facilities, air defenses, and residential areas, with B-2 bombers flattening nuclear labs and warehouses. Iran reports the US targeted Shajarah al-Tayyibah school in Minab, killing 156 students and teachers, and causing 44,750 residential damages in Tehran alone. Military operations within Iran include the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) displaying Khorramshahr-4 ballistic missiles in Tehran's Enghelab Square during patriotic rallies. The IRGC Aerospace Commander warned that if southern neighbors' facilities are used against Iran, they must "say goodbye to oil production in the West Asia region" and threatened immediate, powerful counter-attacks on predetermined targets if any aggression occurs.

Casualties include the execution of Amir-Ali Mir-Jafari, accused of espionage for Israel and setting fire to a mosque in Tehran in January. The internal political situation is characterized by US claims of a "severely split" Iranian government. Iranian officials, including Parliament Speaker Qalibaf, have refused to send a delegation to Pakistan for talks, citing US "inconsistent and unacceptable behavior," and demands the lifting of the naval blockade as a precondition. Iran's Judiciary denied President Trump's claims that eight women are facing execution. The economic impact is significant; Trump claims Iran is collapsing, losing $500 million daily due to the Hormuz blockade, with military and police personnel complaining of unpaid salaries. Oil prices (Brent) have surged above $100/barrel, and there are reports of increased demand for cash from Iranian banks. Iran's leadership maintains it will not negotiate under pressure and is fully prepared for renewed conflict, viewing the blockade as an "act of war" and a ceasefire violation.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations include an airstrike in southern Gaza that killed armed Palestinian Islamic Jihad operatives posing a threat to IDF forces. In southern Lebanon, the Israeli Air Force struck Hezbollah operatives in Qoussair who crossed "forward defense lines" and near Rab al-Thalathine, responding to rocket fire. A damaged statue of Jesus in the Christian village of Debel was replaced by the IDF "in full coordination with the local community," and two soldiers involved in the incident were dismissed from combat duty and sentenced to 30 days in military prison, with six others summoned for clarification. The IDF also opened previously restricted travel routes in southern Israel for Independence Day on April 22.

Casualties: Several IDF soldiers' deaths were commemorated during Israel's Memorial Day, including Sgt. Ofir Eliyahu (Kfir Brigade, fell 11.11.24 in northern Gaza), Sgt. Natan Hai Liar (Duchifat Battalion, fell 7.10.23 in Gaza envelope), and SGT Yishai Pitousi (Golani Brigade, fell 7.10.23). A Mossad agent, referred to as M., died in May 2023 in a boat accident in Italy while on duty, with his operations significantly impacting the campaign against Iran. Home front air defense saw sirens in Kfar Yuval and Ma'ayan Baruch activated due to the interception of a drone from Lebanon. Hezbollah claimed rocket fire on an Israeli artillery position in Kfar Giladi.

Politically, US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee was recalled to Washington for talks at the White House. Strategic objectives are focused on continued military pressure on enemies, including those involved in the October 7 attacks, and preventing existential threats, with PM Netanyahu emphasizing a strong alliance with the US. Independence Day celebrations across Israel included public performances and alternative ceremonies, with President Javier Milei of Argentina participating in the official ceremony.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Ground operations in southern Gaza saw the IDF eliminating armed Palestinian Islamic Jihad operatives who posed an immediate threat to Israeli forces. In the West Bank, near Al-Mughayyir village in the Ramallah area, IDF forces responded to stone-throwing at an Israeli vehicle. A reserve soldier from the vehicle fired at suspects, with reports of five Palestinians injured and two killed.

The humanitarian situation is concerning; Israeli settlers reportedly set up barbed wire along a school route, preventing dozens of Palestinian students from attending classes. Settlers also set fire to a Palestinian family's home, injuring a one-year-old baby. There were no specific updates on ceasefire or negotiation status in Gaza beyond the IDF's targeting of PIJ operatives who "violated the ceasefire understandings." Settler activity, including arson and blocking school access, was reported.

LEBANON
Hezbollah operations included launching rockets at an Israeli artillery position in Kfar Giladi and at IDF troops in the Rab al-Thalathine area in southern Lebanon. A drone was also launched towards Israel, which was intercepted before crossing the border. Hezbollah claimed these actions were a response to "over 200 blatant violations" of the ceasefire by Israeli forces since Friday, asserting its right to resist occupation.

Israeli strikes targeted the rocket launcher used by Hezbollah in Rab al-Thalathine. IAF also struck Hezbollah operatives near Qoussair who had crossed the "forward defense line" and approached IDF forces in a threatening manner, and in the Wadi al-Hujair area (reported by Lebanese media) and Wadi Salouki. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam stated Lebanon would pursue diplomatic solutions through direct talks with Israel, with French President Macron offering assistance to prepare for these negotiations and reiterating that stability in Lebanon requires Israeli withdrawal. The IDF's Northern Command Chief, Maj. Gen. Rafi Milo, stated that hundreds of IDF soldiers are currently operating in Lebanon to remove threats from the north.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Militia activity included "Golani gangs" bringing significant military reinforcements to Al-Ya'rubiya in eastern Hasakah, Syria, following violent clashes with the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) over control of oil wells. Airstrikes by unknown drones targeted the Darashkaran camp in Erbil province, northern Iraq, injuring members of the Democratic Party of Kurdistan. The spillover effects include a Saudi assessment that up to half of the nearly 1,000 drone attacks on Saudi Arabia over the past five weeks originated from inside Iraq. Diplomatically, the US is reportedly blocking the transfer of approximately $500 million in Iraqi oil revenues.

GULF STATES
Pakistan's Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif thanked US President Trump for extending the ceasefire and expressed hope for a comprehensive peace agreement between Iran and the US. A senior Iranian official reported that Pakistan's efforts to persuade the US to lift the naval blockade and release the crew of seized Iranian ships have been unsuccessful. The United Arab Emirates (UAE) embassy in the US reported that Iran launched 2,819 missiles and drones towards the UAE during the conflict. The US is reportedly considering economic aid for the UAE due to financial losses from the war. The European Central Bank (ECB) chief, Christine Lagarde, warned that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is causing significant economic uncertainty and contributing to inflation concerns due to energy supply disruptions. IRGC Aerospace Commander warned Iran's "southern neighbors" that if their geography and facilities are used against the Iranian nation, they "must say goodbye to oil production in the West Asia region." The US Navy is reportedly planning to deploy Patriot missile defense systems on its ships to protect against drones and missiles. Oil prices (Brent) have risen above $100 per barrel.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Ceasefire Extension and Negotiation Standoff:** President Trump extended the ceasefire with Iran at Pakistan's request, but Iran refused to attend planned talks in Islamabad, demanding the immediate lifting of the US naval blockade and release of seized vessels as a precondition.
2.  **US Naval Actions Against Iran:** The US military seized two oil tankers, "Tiffany" and "Touska," in the Indian Ocean and Sea of Oman, accusing them of illicit material support to Iran.
3.  **Hezbollah Ceasefire Violations and IDF Response:** Hezbollah launched rockets at an Israeli artillery position in Kfar Giladi and IDF troops in southern Lebanon, and a drone towards Israel. The IDF retaliated by striking the rocket launcher and Hezbollah operatives.
4.  **Iranian Readiness and Warnings:** Iran's IRGC displayed Khorramshahr-4 ballistic missiles in Tehran and warned that any aggression against Iran or use of southern neighbors' facilities against Iran would lead to severe retaliation, including impacting regional oil production.
5.  **Strait of Hormuz Status:** Trump claimed the US has completely blockaded the Strait of Hormuz, causing Iran $500 million in daily losses, while Iran's Foreign Minister called the blockade an "act of war" and a violation of the ceasefire.
6.  **US Diplomatic Movements:** US Vice President J.D. Vance cancelled his trip to Pakistan for peace talks. Separately, US Ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, was recalled to Washington for discussions at the White House.
7.  **Iran's Internal Situation:** Amir-Ali Mir-Jafari was executed in Iran for alleged espionage for Israel and arson.
8.  **EU Diplomatic Efforts:** Germany and Italy blocked a Spanish-led proposal for the EU to debate suspending its association agreement with Israel. France offered to assist Lebanon in preparing for direct talks with Israel.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are high. The US-Iran ceasefire is extremely fragile, with Iran's firm refusal to engage in talks while the naval blockade persists, coupled with its overt military readiness (missile displays, IRGC warnings). US military commanders have stated readiness for "major combat operations" against Iran. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, where US naval presence and Iranian threats of closure or forceful breaking of the blockade create a high-risk environment. The Lebanon-Israel border remains highly volatile, with frequent cross-border exchanges and Hezbollah claiming over 200 Israeli ceasefire violations to justify its own attacks. Military posture changes include significant depletion of US missile stockpiles in the past weeks of conflict, increased US air transport to the Middle East, and the deployment of Patriot missile systems on US Navy ships. Iran’s stated red lines include the naval blockade, which it considers an "act of war," and any compromise on its nuclear enrichment program.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**US posture:** President Trump extended the ceasefire with Iran but continued the naval blockade and new sanctions on 14 Iran-linked entities. He asserted US military readiness to resume "major combat operations" and claimed Iran had no choice but to negotiate. VP J.D. Vance's trip to Pakistan was paused, and Ambassador Mike Huckabee was recalled from Israel to Washington for White House talks.
**Gulf states:** Pakistan is actively mediating between the US and Iran, with PM Shahbaz Sharif expressing optimism for a comprehensive peace deal. The UAE stated that Iran launched 2,819 missiles and drones against it, and the US is reportedly considering financial aid to the UAE due to war-related economic losses.
**EU members:** Germany and Italy blocked a Spanish, Slovenian, and Irish proposal to debate suspending the EU's association agreement with Israel. French President Macron offered support to Lebanon for direct talks with Israel and emphasized that stability in Lebanon requires Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territories. The ECB chief warned of economic uncertainties caused by the Strait of Hormuz closure.
**Russia:** Russian media (RIA Novosti) cited an Iranian diplomatic source stating that the US seizure of an Iranian commercial vessel was a key reason for Iran's refusal to negotiate.
**China:** China blamed the US for the diplomatic impasse with Iran, urged Washington to show "sincerity" in talks, and warned the US "not to play with fire" following the seizure of a vessel en route from China to Iran.
**Turkey:** The Turkish Ministry of Defense reported a CH-47 Heavy Lift Helicopter crash during a training flight.
**Yemen (Ansarullah):** The Houthi leader, Abdul-Malik al-Houthi, accused Gulf states of suppressing pro-Palestinian sentiment and warned that Yemen would join the conflict if renewed US aggression against Iran occurred.
**UN:** UN Secretary-General welcomed the ceasefire extension, urged parties to avoid undermining it, and called for constructive engagement. Iran formally requested the UN to compel the US to release the commercial vessel Touska and its crew, calling the seizure an "act of piracy."

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Contradictions persist regarding the status of US-Iran negotiations, with Iranian state media (Tasnim, ISNA, State TV) consistently denying that a delegation has departed for Pakistan, while early reports from AP and some Pakistani/Arab sources suggested imminent arrivals. President Trump's statements oscillate between not wanting to extend the ceasefire and then doing so, and claims of a "totally won" war with 13,000 targets destroyed (including nuclear facilities) without civilian casualties are contradicted by Iranian reports of school and residential damage and an ongoing conflict. The IDF initially reported alarms in Kfar Yuval and Ma'ayan Baruch as false alarms, later revising to an actual drone interception and rocket fire. Unverified claims include Trump's specific economic figures for Iran's losses ($500 million/day) and the reported use of "DoniLand" by Ukraine. Propaganda indicators are evident in both US and Iranian rhetoric, with Trump's self-congratulatory language and dismissal of critics contrasting with Iranian state media's focus on nationalistic rallies and vows of revenge. Reporting gaps include the precise terms and duration of the ceasefire, independent verification of claimed military damages, and the full extent of back-channel communications between the US and Iran.
